biography: Pedro Queirolo, a name whispered with respect and a hint of apprehension in the Brazilian racing scene, didn't come from motorsport royalty. Born in the bustling favelas of São Paulo, his initial racing experience was dodging stray dogs and weaving through traffic on a battered scooter. His talent was undeniable, even then. A local mechanic, 'Zé of the Gears,' saw potential and took young Pedro under his wing, teaching him the inner workings of engines and the subtle art of car control. Pedro's first big break came at 19, winning a local karting championship against considerably wealthier competition. This victory caught the attention of JLM Racing, and he was quickly signed to their development program. After a few seasons in Formula Brazil, he made the jump to endurance racing, proving himself a formidable competitor in the MetalMoro MRX P2. Now, at 32, Queirolo has established himself as a force to be reckoned with, known for his cool demeanor and precise execution, a peak driver at the height of his game.
drivingStyle: Queirolo is a calculating driver, often described as an 'ice man' behind the wheel. He doesn't possess the raw, flamboyant aggression of some of his rivals, but compensates with methodical precision. He meticulously analyzes track conditions and tire wear, conserving his equipment for the crucial closing stages of a race. Queirolo excels under pressure, rarely making mistakes when the stakes are high. His corner entry is precise, almost surgical, and he prioritizes exit speed, setting up clean overtaking opportunities. He's a master of tire management, known for consistently delivering faster lap times at the end of a stint than at the beginning.

quirks: Always wears a small, tarnished silver cross given to him by his grandmother before every race.
Insists on personally polishing his helmet visor before each session, no matter how clean it already is.
Listens to the same vintage samba album on repeat in the hours leading up to a race to calm his nerves.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about brute force; it's about finding the rhythm, understanding the machine, and knowing when to strike.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2020 Brazilian Endurance Championship after a nail-biting final race at Interlagos, where he secured the title with a last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2019 São Paulo 500 after a mechanical failure, costing him a guaranteed victory and severely damaging his championship hopes.
